explain.say: The Baha'i Faith began in Iran in the 1800s. Its founder, Baha'u'llah, taught that there is one God, that the great religions come from that one God, and that humanity is one family.

explain.say: Baha'is believe God sends messengers in every age, such as Abraham, Moses, the Buddha, Jesus and the Prophet Muhammad, each bringing teaching suited to their time. This is called progressive revelation.

items: Muhammad, then the Bab and Baha'u'llah

explain.say: Unity is the heart of the faith. Baha'is work for the oneness of humanity, equality of women and men, harmony of science and religion, education for all, and an end to prejudice.
There are no priests. Baha'is pray daily, fast for nineteen days each March, and meet every nineteen days for a feast. Their Houses of Worship have nine sides and are open to people of every faith.

faq.q: What do Baha'is believe about unity?
faq.a: Baha'is believe in the oneness of God, the oneness of religion and the oneness of humanity. They see all people as one family, and work to end prejudice of race, class, religion and nation.
asks: What is the oneness of humanity?

faq.a: Baha'u'llah, meaning the Glory of God, was born in Tehran in 1817 and founded the Baha'i Faith. Baha'is believe he is the latest messenger of God. He was exiled for his teachings and died near Akka in 1892.

The Bab, meaning the Gate, was a young merchant from Shiraz in Iran who in 1844 announced that a new messenger of God would soon appear. He was executed in 1850. Baha'is honour him as a messenger who prepared the way for Baha'u'llah.

faq.q: Why is Haifa important to Baha'is?
faq.a: Haifa and nearby Akka in Israel are home to the Baha'i World Centre. The Shrine of the Bab, with its golden dome and terraced gardens on Mount Carmel, is in Haifa, and the Shrine of Baha'u'llah, the holiest Baha'i place, is near Akka.
asks: What is the Baha'i World Centre?

faq.a: It is the Baha'i belief that God reveals truth step by step through messengers in different ages, such as Abraham, Krishna, Moses, Zoroaster, the Buddha, Jesus and the Prophet Muhammad, followed by the Bab and Baha'u'llah.
asks: Do Baha'is believe in all religions?

faq.q: What is the Baha'i holy book?
faq.a: The most important book is the Kitab-i-Aqdas, the Most Holy Book, written by Baha'u'llah. Other writings include the Book of Certitude and the Hidden Words, and the writings of the Bab and Abdu'l-Baha are also sacred.
No. The Baha'i Faith has no clergy. Communities are run by elected councils called Spiritual Assemblies, and worldwide by the Universal House of Justice in Haifa, elected every five years.
asks: What is the Universal House of Justice?

faq.q: What is a Baha'i House of Worship?
faq.a: A Baha'i House of Worship is a nine-sided building with a dome, open to people of all religions to pray and reflect. There are no sermons; scriptures of many faiths are read or sung. The Lotus Temple in New Delhi is a famous one.
asks: Why do Baha'i temples have nine sides?

faq.q: Why is nine important to Baha'is?
faq.a: Nine is the highest single digit, and Baha'is see it as a symbol of completeness and unity. That is why their Houses of Worship have nine sides, and a nine-pointed star is a common Baha'i symbol.
Yes. Adult Baha'is fast from sunrise to sunset for nineteen days in March, the last month of the Baha'i year. The fast ends with Naw-Ruz, the Baha'i new year, around the spring equinox.
The Baha'i calendar has 19 months of 19 days each, plus a few extra days. Every nineteen days Baha'is gather for the Nineteen Day Feast, with prayer, community news and friendship.
asks: What is the Nineteen Day Feast?
How many months in the Baha'i year?

faq.q: What do Baha'is believe about women and men?
faq.a: Baha'is believe women and men are equal. Baha'u'llah's son Abdu'l-Baha compared humanity to a bird with two wings, one female and one male, which can only fly when both are strong.
asks: Equality of women in the Baha'i Faith

faq.a: Estimates usually say several million, often about 5 to 8 million, living in almost every country. It is one of the most widely spread religions geographically.
asks: Number of Baha'is in the world?

facts: Baha'u'llah, founder of the Baha'i Faith, was born in Tehran in 1817 and died near Akka in 1892.
The Bab announced his mission in 1844.
The Baha'i World Centre is in Haifa and Akka in Israel.
Baha'i Houses of Worship have nine sides and are open to people of all faiths.
The Baha'i calendar has 19 months of 19 days.
